## Workflow A — Ingestion & Identity

Four channel entry points normalize to one common schema, then resolve identity against HubSpot:
phone match → volunteered email in message → (if still unresolved) proceed with reply, explicit ask deferred to meeting/quote step in Workflow B → on eventual email match, check phone conflict before merging.

Output of this workflow is the contract Workflow B consumes. Do not change field names below without updating B.

nodes.name: Guard - Drop Malformed WhatsApp
nodes.notes: Explicit fail-loud per Rule 5 instead of silently passing a broken payload downstream.

nodes.name: HubSpot - Search by Phone
nodes.notes: Using HTTP Request against the CRM Search API (not the native HubSpot node) because the native node's contact search doesn't support arbitrary property filters — the search API does. This is the one deliberate non-default node choice worth flagging (Rule 12).

nodes.name: Set - Resolved via Phone
nodes.notes: NOTE for review: the source-item reference here needs to point at the actual upstream normalized item for whichever channel triggered this run, not a hardcoded node name. In n8n this is handled by keeping the normalized fields flowing through the HubSpot HTTP node untouched (HTTP Request only appends its own response fields) rather than by an explicit $('NodeName') reference — flagging this as a known rough edge to verify once wired up in the live editor, not something to treat as already correct (Rule 3).

nodes.name: Flag for Manual Review
nodes.notes: incoming phone did not match the existing contact's phone on record. Needs manual review.

nodes.name: Create New Contact
nodes.notes: Reached both when no email was found in the message (create with phone only) and when volunteered email search found no match (create with both). Contact created with whatever identifiers are actually available — creation is never blocked on having both (matches the agreed no-hard-gate decision).

nodes.name: Log Engagement to HubSpot
nodes.notes: This IS the conversation-memory mechanism (Design step 3) and the audit log (Rule 6) in one write — no separate logging system needed.

nodes.name: IF - Email Conflict
nodes.notes: True only when BOTH: a new email was given/extracted this turn AND it differs from what's on file. If no new email was given this turn, contact_email is empty and this correctly falls to false — no conflict, nothing to do, just an existing email with no new info.

nodes.name: Flag Email Conflict for Review
nodes.notes: Per Rule 5: don't silently overwrite an existing email — people do sometimes deliberately switch, but this could also be a typo or a shared phone. Flag, don't guess.

nodes.name: IF - New Email Given
nodes.notes: Reached only when existing_email was empty — checks whether this turn actually supplied one to add.

nodes.name: If A - IF Has Phone Conflict

workflowId.cachedResultName: Workflow B - Agent Core (Slice 1: History + Knowledge Retrieval only)

nodes.name: Call 'Workflow B - Agent Core (Slice 1: History + Knowledge Retrieval only)'
WhatsApp Webhook Trigger1
nodes.notes: Meta requires the same URL to answer a GET verification challenge (hub.challenge) AND receive POST messages. Branch below splits these two cases — this is non-obvious and worth flagging (Rule 12).

nodes.name: HubSpot - Search by Session ID
nodes.notes: Using HTTP Request against the CRM Search API (not the native HubSpot node) because the native node's contact search doesn't support arbitrary property filters — the search API does. This is the one deliberate non-default node choice worth flagging (Rule 12).

nodes.name: Flag Phone Conflict for Review (Session)
nodes.notes: Per Rule 5: don't silently overwrite an existing email — people do sometimes deliberately switch, but this could also be a typo or a shared phone. Flag, don't guess.
